newsitem.title: INDIA: India relaxes external commercial borrowing rules.
newsitem.headline: India relaxes external commercial borrowing rules.

text.p: The Indian government said on Friday that it was relaxing some restrictions on external commercial borrowings (ECBs) for infrastructure and project financing.
It said in a statement that normally ECBs can account for up to 35 percent of the total cost of all infrastructure and greenfield projects.
"In case of telecom projects, 50 percent of the project cost (including the licence fee) will be allowed as a matter of course," the statement said.
It said that greater flexibility used to be allowed in the case of power projects. "Now it has been decided to extend this flexibility to other infrastructure projects also, on merit," it said.

The statement said that currently ECBs for project financing, or non-recourse financing, could carry a larger interest rate spread above the London Interbank Offered Rate (LIBOR) or U.S. Treasuries than ordinary ECBs.
"Ordinarily a spread of up to 350 basis points may be allowed," it said. "However, keeping market conditions in mind, some flexibility will be permitted in determining the spread on merit."
Earlier, a Finance Ministry official said the government had decided to remove the ceiling on ECBs with maturities of more than 10 years.
